subtype: Approach: pairing the hobby with an existing habit [Thinking]
passage: Chinmayi dropped her school bag. "I keep forgetting to read," she told her father Mohit, who was folding laundry. "Every night I say I will start, and then I am asleep." "Hmm," said Mohit. "What is the one thing I never forget?" she asked herself aloud. "Brushing my teeth. Every night, even when I am sleepy." Mohit raised an eyebrow. "So if I read right after brushing... the brushing reminds me!" "Try it," said Mohit. That night she put her story book on the shelf by the mirror, brushed, then sat on the bed with it. A week later Mohit said, "You did not even remind yourself tonight." "Brush, then book," said Chinmayi, grinning.

qa.q: Where did Chinmayi put her story book?
qa.a: She put it on the shelf by the mirror.

qa.q: What was Chinmayi feeling at the start about her reading?
qa.a: Frustrated with herself, since she kept saying she would begin and then fell asleep.

qa.q: What else could Chinmayi use as a cue for the habit?
qa.a: She could read right after packing her bag for the next day, because attaching a new habit to a daily one makes it easier to remember.

qa.q: How might Mohit see the new habit?
qa.a: With quiet pride, since he noticed she no longer needed reminding. 🙂

grounding: A girl attaches reading to brushing her teeth at night, a task she already does daily, so it is easier to remember.

subtype: Approach: pairing the hobby with an existing habit [Thinking]
passage: I'm Bhavna, and I'm bad at remembering things that aren't already part of my day. I got a thick story book for my birthday and kept forgetting it under my bed. Then I noticed something. I never forget to brush my teeth at night, because "Brushing done, beti?" comes from Mummy every night and my sister Mehak stands at the basin tapping her foot. So I thought, what if the book lives right next to my toothbrush? Brush, then read. The toothbrush can remind me. Now the book sits on the bathroom shelf beside the toothpaste. When I finish brushing I pick it up and read two chapters in bed. Mehak says it's weird to keep a book in the bathroom. It is a bit weird, but I'm on chapter nine.

qa.q: Where does the book sit now?
qa.a: It sits on the bathroom shelf beside the toothpaste.

qa.q: How did Bhavna feel about the forgotten book before the new plan?
qa.a: Bhavna felt a bit frustrated about forgetting a birthday book under the bed, and wanted a way to remember that didn't rely on willpower.

qa.q: What else could Bhavna attach reading to if bedtime gets rushed?
qa.a: Another thing done every day without fail, like breakfast or the bus ride home, as long as the book is kept right next to it.

qa.q: How does Mehak see the new habit?
qa.a: Mehak finds a book in the bathroom weird and teases about it, but the habit rides on the brushing she already makes sure happens.

grounding: A girl explains attaching her new reading habit to brushing her teeth at night so it is easy to remember.

subtype: Approach: pairing the hobby with an existing habit [Thinking]
passage:
Class 3B reading log, teacher's note, 12 November
Parveen's reading log was empty for most of October. When I asked why, she said she kept forgetting at home. Last week she came to me with her own idea: "I brush my teeth every night without forgetting. So I'll read right after brushing, before lights off." She drew a toothbrush next to the word READ on her log. This week there are six ticks out of seven, each with a book title. She told the class about it during circle time, and two others want to try it. I have given her a bookmark shaped like a toothbrush, which made her laugh. Please keep a book near the basin at home for her.
— Vikas, class teacher

qa.q: How many ticks are on Parveen's log this week?
qa.a: There are six ticks out of seven, each with a book title.

qa.q: How might Parveen have felt coming to the teacher with her own idea?
qa.a: She was probably proud and hopeful, having worked out a way to stop forgetting that came from her own daily routine.

qa.q: What should Parveen do if she misses a night?
qa.a: Simply pick it up again the next night after brushing, rather than giving up, because the brushing cue will still be there.

qa.q: How does Vikas seem to see Parveen's plan?
qa.a: Vikas seems pleased, rewarding it with a toothbrush bookmark and asking the family to back it at home 👍.

grounding: A teacher's note shows a girl tying reading to brushing her teeth at night so the new habit is easy to remember.
